name: git-if
desc: Glulx interpreter that is optimized for speed
why: A speed-optimized Glulx interpreter opens the interactive fiction world, a deep old-school environment for the curious.

brief.what_it_is: Git is an interpreter for the Glulx virtual machine, a runtime for interactive fiction story files. According to IFWiki it was written by Iain Merrick and is now maintained by David Kinder. It takes a Glulx game file and runs it in a console or window, showing the game's text and reading the player's input. The IF Archive index lists source for Git 1.3.8, a Windows console build, a Windows Glk build, and older MS-DOS and PocketPC builds. IFWiki notes that the interpreter cannot simply be downloaded and run to play game files, so you need to supply a story file.
brief.why_it_exists: The IF Archive describes it simply as Iain Merrick's Git, a Glulx interpreter that is optimized for speed. IFWiki adds that it may be significantly faster than Glulxe, the other common Glulx interpreter.
brief.install_notes: Beyond the brew formula, you need a Glulx story file (a game) to play, since the interpreter does not come with games. The archive offers prebuilt Windows binaries (wingit-138.zip, which uses Windows Glk 1.55, and a Windows console build of 1.3.5 compiled with PDCurses) and the 1.3.8 source as git-138.zip. I did not find build steps or a README in the pages I read, so compile requirements are unknown. The Homebrew executable is named git-if; I did not verify how it maps to the upstream binary.
brief.standout: It is an old-school Glulx interpreter, and its selling point is raw speed compared with Glulxe. IFWiki says it is used by several other IF tools, including CellarDoor, Emglken, Frotz for iOS, Gargoyle, and Windows Git, so it works as a shared engine under other front ends.
brief.status: quiet. The latest release is 1.3.8, dated 12 October 2023 on the IF Archive, and IFWiki lists it as Stable with David Kinder as a developer. IFWiki's page was last edited 7 March 2024. The archive's Windows 1.3.8 build is listed as 23-Aug-2026, which is the newest date in the index. I did not check the upstream commit history.
brief.caveats: The brew description and the archive both say it is for playing Glulx games, so it is not useful on its own. IFWiki warns that the name collides with the version control system Git, which is used to develop many IF projects, so search results can be confusing. The original Git homepage is offline as of 2014, according to IFWiki, so the IF Archive is the main source. Platform support is listed as Unix, Windows, and PocketPC, and the DOS and PocketPC builds are old (2004). The IFWiki infobox lists the license as MIT.
quotes: a Glulx interpreter that is optimized for speed.
